interactions.summary: Students describe art as self-dissolution, dialogue, temporal escape, and resonance with the dead; Jiang consolidates these into unity beyond time and space and briefly names Walter Benjamin's aura.

claims.claim: Jiang accepts the student's account of art-viewing as an oscillation among viewer, artist, subject, and object, calling it a dialogue or simulation that tries to bring self and painting together.
Jiang pushes that imaginative art-experience can move a viewer outside ordinary time and space, producing a felt unity rather than separation.
In the Oxford portraits example, Jiang accepts the idea that paintings can transmit the lingering memory or soul-presence of earlier lives, creating awe and resonance across generations.
Jiang briefly invokes Walter Benjamin's term aura to name the living energy or personality an artwork acquires through long audience participation and then reflects back into the viewer.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang condenses the student's mystical account into a strong formula: time and space create separation, but moving outside them creates unity.
signature_moments.source_phrase: Time and space create separation, but once you move out of time and space, it creates unity
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is one of the lecture's clearest metaphysical statements about how art heals fragmentation.

signature_moments.moment: Aura appears as Jiang's name for the artwork's quasi-living energy, built up across centuries of human attention.
signature_moments.source_phrase: Every artwork has its own aura
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It ties the classroom phenomenology of art to a named theoretical tradition without losing Jiang's own emphasis on aliveness.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Borrowed from Walter Benjamin, aura names the artwork's accumulated personality or energy produced through centuries of audience participation.

chronology_notes.note: The lecture deepens its imagination theory into a metaphysical one: art can suspend ordinary separation, create unity, and transmit presence across time.

uncertainty_notes.note: Jiang's casual location reference for the Last Supper appears unstable in the transcript and should not be treated as a reliable factual claim; the substantive point is the aura argument.
